A default administrator that cannot administer is not one.

in: BOOT-5a: in the SAME first-boot transaction that creates the identities, create their role bindings -- nexusadmin with full administrative capability per ROLE-1, claudeadmin with role:viewer and nothing else per ROLE-3.

Use the role vocabulary UI2_0_C3_IDENTITY_SESSIONS_RBAC_CONTRACT.md section 5 already defines. Do not invent a role name, and do not invent a 'superadmin' -- C3 has none. Full administrative capability means the existing roles that together give it; state in the SESSION_CLOSE exactly which ones you bound and why that set is 'full'.

A local identity's role binding references itself rather than a directory group, per C3A section 7.1 and the existing bootstrap-security-admin CLI path. Follow whatever that path already does rather than inventing a second shape.
BOOT-4 extends to the bindings: each binding row is audited through C1 section 3.5's existing trigger under the same reserved bootstrap actor marker the identity creation uses.

BOOT-2's idempotence must continue to hold and must now cover bindings as well: if local_credentials holds any row the runner still does nothing at all, so a restart neither reseeds an identity nor re-creates or overwrites a binding.
BOOT-5b: the existing deployment-controlled CLI paths keep working unchanged, and remain the way a binding is created or changed outside first boot.

changed: FirstBootIdentitySeedingRunner now seeds each bootstrap identity's role binding(s) in the same transaction as the identity row, via new FirstBootIdentityRoleBindingSeeder (ui2/persistence/.../identity).

nexusadmin is bound to every role token in C3 section 4.1's closed vocabulary: role:viewer, role:operator, role:onboarding_admin, role:backup_admin, role:compliance_admin, role:security_admin. This is 'full administrative capability' (ROLE-1): C3 section 4.1 states no token implies another by hierarchy, so full capability is the union of every token bound individually; binding role:security_admin alongside execution tokens on one identity would normally trip C3's separation-of-duties rule, but ROLE-2 explicitly places the bootstrap administrator outside that rule.
claudeadmin is bound only to role:viewer (ROLE-3), nothing else.

Each local identity's binding is direct and self-referencing (C3A section 7.1): group_reference_encrypted holds the identity's own local_identity_id, encrypted under the existing role_bindings envelope (GroupReferenceCipher).

LocalAuthenticationConfiguration now wires a RoleBindingRepository bean and a GroupReferenceCipher bean (reading a new required secret file, C1 section 6.2 <VAR>_FILE convention) so the running service can encrypt/write role_bindings at first boot; application.yml gained ui2.role-binding.group-reference-key-file / group-reference-key-id.

Removed the now-unused LocalIdentityBootstrapPort Spring bean from LocalAuthenticationConfiguration (the runner no longer goes through it; the CLI path composes its own instance independently of Spring and is unaffected).
Updated FirstBootIdentitySeedingRunnerTest and FirstBootIdentitySeedingIntegrationTest to cover the new binding behavior, including one new decisive test proving RBAC resolution.

unresolved_risks: The decisive test (AC-1/AC-2) was not executed against the prior merged code in this session -- reverting cleanly mid-edit was judged riskier than the alternative. Failure against prior code was instead established by source inspection: the prior FirstBootIdentitySeedingRunner never referenced RoleBindingRepository, and RbacEvaluator.evaluate(...) returns AUTHZ_NOT_EVALUATED(role_token_unbound) whenever zero active bindings exist for a token -- a logical certainty, not an executed observation, and reported as such per the UNKNOWN/fail-closed law.

The true single-transaction guarantee (AC-3) rests on jOOQ's default ThreadLocalTransactionProvider nesting nested transactionResult(...) calls as savepoints when repositories share one DSLContext/Configuration -- verified by reading JooqTransactionBoundary/JooqRoleBindingRepository/JooqLocalCredentialsRepository and confirming they all resolve to the same singleton bean, but not proven by a real-database test in this sandbox (no Docker/UI2_TEST_JDBC_URL here). FirstBootIdentitySeedingIntegrationTest was updated to prove this against a real PostgreSQL 16 instance and compiles cleanly, but could not be executed in this environment.
